name: Midpoint reversal with spread hurdle
note: Short-horizon reversal computed on the log range midpoint eta = (ln H + ln L)/2 instead of on the closing transaction price, and gated by a bid-ask spread estimated from the same bars. The estimator is the Abdi-Ranaldo two-day corrected form exactly as the idea states it, S_i = mean over the trailing mr_win bars of sqrt(max((c_d - eta_d)(c_d - eta_{d+1}), 0)), with the round-trip spread 2*S_i; the term for bar d needs eta_{d+1}, so it only enters S once bar d+1 has closed, which keeps it causal. Signal MR = eta_t - eta_{t-mr_look}, entry long on negative MR and short on positive, but only when |MR| both ranks above its own trailing mr_pct-th percentile and exceeds mr_cost * S_i. Exit is the harness time stop at mr_look bars, plus the family's own two: eta crossing back through its mr_win-bar mean (target reached) and the estimated spread more than doubling since entry. ONE SUBSTANTIAL DEVIATION, stated plainly: the idea is cross-sectional (demean MR across the liquid universe, take the 10 most extreme names per side) and this study runs one symbol at a time, so the cross-sectional demean is replaced by a demean against the symbol's own trailing mr_dm-bar mean of MR, and the 'most extreme names' selection by a trailing percentile of |MRdm| on the same symbol. What survives intact is the part the idea calls novel - the signal never touches a closing transaction price, and entry is priced against an OHLCV-estimated round trip. What is lost is the market-neutrality of the cross-sectional book. One measured caveat that matters for reading results: on 5-minute bars the estimated half-spread is 0.7 bp of log price on SPY and 8.5 bp on SOXL, while |MRdm| at the extreme bars is 10x to 500x that (median 20-25x), so the idea's stated 4x hurdle rejects literally nothing on a single symbol - in the paper the hurdle does its work by discriminating BETWEEN names of different spread, which a one-symbol test cannot reproduce. The default is therefore set at 16x, which rejects about half the candidates, and the grid keeps 4x so the non-binding case is measured rather than assumed.
source: Stefan Nagel, 'Evaporating Liquidity', NBER WP 17653 (2011) / RFS 25 (2012) 2005-2039 - the transaction-price-versus-midpoint decomposition of short-horizon reversal. Farshid Abdi & Angelo Ranaldo, 'A simple estimation of bid-ask spreads from daily close, high, and low prices', RFS 30 (2017) 4437-4480, building on Corwin & Schultz, JF 67 (2012) and Roll, JF 39 (1984).

import math as _m


def family_init(ctx):
    bars = ctx.bars
    n = len(bars)
    look = max(1, int(ctx.p.mr_look))
    N = max(5, int(ctx.p.mr_win))
    cost = max(0.0, float(ctx.p.mr_cost))
    dm = max(20, int(ctx.p.mr_dm))
    pct = min(99.0, max(0.0, float(ctx.p.mr_pct))) / 100.0

    # log range midpoint -- the efficient-price proxy the whole idea rests on
    eta = [None] * n
    lc = [None] * n
    for i in range(n):
        h = float(bars[i]["h"])
        l = float(bars[i]["l"])
        c = float(bars[i]["c"])
        if h > 0.0 and l > 0.0 and c > 0.0:
            eta[i] = 0.5 * (_m.log(h) + _m.log(l))
            lc[i] = _m.log(c)

    # Abdi-Ranaldo two-day corrected term for each bar d: needs eta_{d+1},
    # so the term for d is only available once bar d+1 has closed.
    term = [None] * n
    for d in range(n - 1):
        if eta[d] is None or lc[d] is None or eta[d + 1] is None:
            continue
        x = (lc[d] - eta[d]) * (lc[d] - eta[d + 1])
        term[d] = _m.sqrt(x) if x > 0.0 else 0.0

    # S_i averages the terms for d = i-N .. i-1, all of which are known at i
    sp = [None] * n
    run = 0.0
    cnt = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        d = i - 1
        if term[d] is not None:
            run += term[d]
            cnt += 1
        old = i - 1 - N
        if old >= 0 and term[old] is not None:
            run -= term[old]
            cnt -= 1
        if cnt >= N // 2 and i > N:
            sp[i] = run / cnt

    # midpoint reversal, demeaned against its own trailing mean (the study is
    # single-symbol, so the cross-sectional demean is replaced by a time-series
    # one -- see the note)
    mr = [None] * n
    for i in range(look, n):
        if eta[i] is not None and eta[i - look] is not None:
            mr[i] = eta[i] - eta[i - look]
    mrd = [None] * n
    run = 0.0
    cnt = 0
    for i in range(n):
        if mr[i] is not None:
            run += mr[i]
            cnt += 1
        o = i - dm
        if o >= 0 and mr[o] is not None:
            run -= mr[o]
            cnt -= 1
        if mr[i] is not None and cnt >= dm // 2 and i >= dm:
            mrd[i] = mr[i] - run / cnt

    # |MRdm| must be extreme in its own recent history -- the time-series
    # stand-in for "the 10 most extreme names on each side"
    _ratios = []
    sig = [0] * n
    n_ext = 0
    n_pass = 0
    for i in range(n):
        x = mrd[i]
        s = sp[i]
        if x is None or s is None or i < dm:
            continue
        a = abs(x)
        lo = i - dm
        below = 0
        tot = 0
        for k in range(lo, i):
            y = mrd[k]
            if y is not None:
                tot += 1
                if abs(y) <= a:
                    below += 1
        if tot < dm // 2 or below < pct * tot:
            continue
        n_ext += 1
        _ratios.append(a / s if s > 0 else 0.0)
        if a <= cost * s:
            continue
        n_pass += 1
        sig[i] = 1 if x < 0.0 else -1

    ctx.mr_s = ctx.series(sig, "midpoint_reversal")
    ctx.mr_e = ctx.series(eta, "log_midpoint")
    ctx.mr_p = ctx.series(sp, "ar_half_spread")
    mm = [None] * n
    run = 0.0
    cnt = 0
    for i in range(n):
        if eta[i] is not None:
            run += eta[i]
            cnt += 1
        o = i - N
        if o >= 0 and eta[o] is not None:
            run -= eta[o]
            cnt -= 1
        if cnt > 0 and i >= N:
            mm[i] = run / cnt
    ctx.mr_m = ctx.series(mm, "midpoint_mean")
    ok = [v for v in sp if v is not None]
    if ok:
        q = sorted(ok)
        ctx.log("AR half-spread med %.5f (%.1f bp of a log price); %d extreme "
                "bars, %d cleared the %.1fx cost hurdle"
                % (q[len(q) // 2], 1e4 * q[len(q) // 2], n_ext, n_pass, cost))
    if _ratios:
        r = sorted(_ratios)
        ctx.log("|MRdm|/S at extreme bars: p05 %.1f p25 %.1f med %.1f p75 %.1f max %.1f"
                % (r[len(r)//20], r[len(r)//4], r[len(r)//2], r[3*len(r)//4], r[-1]))


def signal(ctx, i):
    s = ctx.mr_s[i]
    return s if s else 0


def exit_signal(ctx, i):
    """Target reached (midpoint back through its own mean), or the spread blew out."""
    if not ctx.positions:
        return False
    e = ctx.mr_e[i]
    m = ctx.mr_m[i]
    p = ctx.positions[0]
    if e is not None and m is not None:
        if p["side"] == "long" and e > m:
            return True
        if p["side"] == "short" and e < m:
            return True
    s = ctx.mr_p[i]
    s0 = ctx.mr_p[p["entry_i"]]
    if s is not None and s0 is not None and s0 > 0.0 and s > 2.0 * s0:
        return True
    return False
